model.name: Equilibrium and adjustment from a price below equilibrium (seed packets)
model.status: uses the existing card's data unchanged; straight lines through the three given points
assumptions: Basic competitive model: price can adjust; the curves do not shift.

question.title: Seed-packet demand and supply schedule
question.description: Table: at N$10, N$20 and N$30 a packet, weekly demand is 90, 60 and 30 packets and weekly supply is 30, 60 and 90 packets. Instruction to draw D and S, mark the equilibrium and show the change towards it from N$10.

static.title: Weekly demand and supply of seed packets

text: Draw D and S on labelled axes, mark the equilibrium
and show the change towards it from N$10.

answer.title: Equilibrium, the shortage at N$10 and the upward price adjustment
answer.description: D through (90, N$10), (60, N$20), (30, N$30) and S through (30, N$10), (60, N$20), (90, N$30) cross at E: N$20 and 60 packets a week, projected to both axes. At N$10 quantity supplied is 30 and quantity demanded 90, an excess demand (shortage) of 60. Arrows along both curves show price rising towards E: quantity demanded contracts and quantity supplied extends.

text: E: N$20 a packet and 60 packets a week (D = S)
At N$10: supplied 30, demanded 90, excess demand 60
Price is pushed up towards N$20: quantity demanded
contracts along D, quantity supplied extends along S

static.text: The shortage at N$10 closes as price rises to E.
